name: G42

summary.text: G42 is an Abu Dhabi artificial-intelligence and cloud-computing group founded in 2018, chaired since 2021 by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE's national security adviser, with Peng Xiao as chief executive; its investors include Mubadala and Silver Lake. In January 2024 the chairman of the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party asked the Commerce Department to examine G42 for the Entity List over alleged ties to Huawei, BGI and Chinese military-linked firms, which G42 denied. In April 2024 Microsoft invested $1.5 billion for a minority stake, with Brad Smith joining G42's board. G42 co-founded the investment firm MGX with Mubadala in 2024. In May 2025 G42, OpenAI, Oracle, Nvidia, SoftBank and Cisco announced Stargate UAE, a 1-gigawatt cluster within a 5-gigawatt UAE-U.S. AI campus in Abu Dhabi, and on November 19, 2025 the Commerce Department authorized G42 to buy the equivalent of up to 35,000 Nvidia Blackwell chips subject to security conditions.

facts.claim: G42 was founded in 2018 and has been chaired since 2021 by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE's national security adviser; its chief executive is Peng Xiao, and its key investors are Abu Dhabi's sovereign fund Mubadala and the U.S. private-equity firm Silver Lake.
facts.quote: Founded in 2018, G42 has been chaired by Sheikh Tahnoun since 2021. G42's key investors are the Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund Mubadala along with U.S. private equity firm Silver Lake.

sources.title: What To Know About G42—The Emirati AI Giant That Just Got A $1.5 Billion Investment From Microsoft
Microsoft invests $1.5 billion in AI firm G42 which faces U.S. scrutiny for China ties

facts.claim: In a letter dated January 3, 2024 to Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo, Rep. Mike Gallagher, then chairman of the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, asked Commerce to examine G42 and 13 subsidiaries and affiliates, including G42 Shanghai Investment Co., Inception Institute of Artificial Intelligence, Presight AI and Hayat BioTech, for inclusion on the Bureau of Industry and Security's Entity List, alleging relationships with Huawei and BGI and that CEO Peng Xiao was affiliated with companies supporting Chinese military-civil fusion. G42 said it categorically denied the claims. The letter states allegations, not findings.
facts.quote: The letter calls on Commerce to closely examine G42 and its subsidiaries for inclusion on the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) Entity List.

facts.claim: On April 16, 2024, Microsoft announced a $1.5 billion strategic investment in G42 for a minority stake. Under the expanded partnership, Microsoft vice chair and president Brad Smith joined G42's board, G42 agreed to run its AI applications and services on Microsoft Azure, and the two companies said they would set up a $1 billion fund for developers.
facts.quote: As part of this expanded partnership Brad Smith, Vice Chair and President of Microsoft, will join the G42 Board of Directors.

sources.title: Microsoft invests $1.5 billion in Abu Dhabi's G42 to accelerate AI development and global expansion
Microsoft and G42 partner to accelerate AI innovation in UAE and beyond

facts.claim: Press reports said the Microsoft investment followed negotiation with the Biden administration and that G42 had agreed to remove Huawei hardware from its AI infrastructure; Bloomberg reported that G42 had reached an understanding with the U.S. Commerce Department in 2023 to scale back its presence in China. Peng Xiao later said that all of G42's previous China investments had been divested.
facts.quote: as part of the deal, G42 reportedly agreed to remove hardware made by Huawei Technologies Co. Ltd. from its artificial intelligence infrastructure.

facts.claim: In July 2024, House Select Committee chairman John Moolenaar and House Foreign Affairs chairman Michael McCaul wrote to National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan requesting a classified briefing and an Intelligence Community assessment of G42's ties to the Chinese Communist Party and People's Liberation Army before any transfer of sensitive technology under the Microsoft partnership. The letter states concerns and requests, not findings.
facts.quote: They asked that the National Intelligence Council prepare an official Intelligence Community assessment on the ties between G42, including its subsidiaries and affiliates, to the CCP, the People's Liberation Army, or any part of the PRC's apparatus.

facts.claim: In May 2025 G42, OpenAI, Oracle, Nvidia, SoftBank Group and Cisco announced Stargate UAE, a 1-gigawatt AI compute cluster to be built by G42's Khazna Data Centers within a 5-gigawatt UAE-U.S. AI campus in Abu Dhabi and operated by OpenAI and Oracle, with Nvidia supplying Grace Blackwell GB300 systems. The first 200-megawatt phase was planned for 2026; G42 said in October 2025 that construction was well underway.
facts.quote: The facility, being developed by Khazna Data Centers, a G42 company, forms part of the 5GW UAE-US AI Campus and is scheduled to go live in 2026.

sources.title: G42 Provides Update on Construction of Stargate UAE AI Infrastructure Cluster
OpenAI, Oracle and NVIDIA will help build Stargate UAE AI campus launching in 2026

facts.claim: On November 19, 2025 the Commerce Department announced it had authorized the export of advanced U.S. semiconductors to G42 and to Saudi Arabia's Humain, each approved to purchase the equivalent of up to 35,000 Nvidia Blackwell GB300 chips, conditioned on security and reporting requirements monitored by the Bureau of Industry and Security. G42's CEO said the company gave security assurances that the chips could not be shipped elsewhere and had no back door for remote access.
facts.quote: Both companies are receiving approvals to purchase the equivalent of up to 35,000 Nvidia Blackwell chips (GB300s).

sources.title: Statement on UAE and Saudi Chip Exports
Abu Dhabi's G42 secures Nvidia chips but says needs far more

facts.claim: Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi, ranking member of the House Select Committee on the CCP, said on May 13, 2025 that reported UAE and Saudi chip deals would allow access to the most advanced chips with limited oversight, and after the November 2025 authorization called the export of tens of thousands of advanced chips to Saudi and UAE firms with ties to Beijing an 'extraordinary national security mistake'. These are the member's stated views, not findings.
facts.quote: He called the decision to authorize the export of tens of thousands of the world's most advanced AI chips to Saudi and UAE firms with deep ties to Beijing an extraordinary national security mistake.

openQuestions: The date of the Gallagher letter is given as January 3, 2024 (file name) and January 9, 2024 (press release); the PDF should be checked.
Whether the Microsoft deal's Huawei-removal and oversight provisions are stated in any official Microsoft or U.S. government document, rather than press reports, was not confirmed.

Reports that G42 executives helped manage a vehicle (Aryam Investment 1) that invested in World Liberty Financial in January 2025 rest on a single secondary summary of a WSJ report and are not recorded here.

A report that a July 10, 2026 Federal Register notice moved the UAE to a more favorable export tier allowing G42 to buy chips without individual licenses was found in one outlet only and is not recorded.
G42's own corporate pages were not opened; the company description comes from Forbes and CNBC.
